title: feat(plugins): add json_prune plugin to strip unnecessary fields from tool output
summary:
## 🔗 Related Issue                                                                     
  Closes #2971
  ---                                                                                     

  ## 📝 Summary
  Adds a `json_prune` plugin that strips unnecessary JSON fields from API tool responses  
  using a whitelist approach. Many REST APIs return noisy data (thumbnails, engines,      
  parsed_urls, etc.) that wastes tokens and can confuse the LLM. This plugin runs as a    
  `tool_post_invoke` hook — only fields explicitly listed in dot-notation paths are       
  retained.

  Based on the implementation proposed by @alex9434 in #2971 and discussion #2511, adapted
   to match project conventions (immutable payloads, proper logging, dual result format   
  support).

  ---

  ## 🏷️ Type of Change
  - [ ] Bug fix
  - [x] Feature / Enhancement
  - [ ] Documentation
  - [ ] Refactor
  - [ ] Chore (deps, CI, tooling)
  - [ ] Other (describe below)

  ---

  ## 🧪 Verification

  | Check                     | Command         | Status |
  |---------------------------|-----------------|--------|
  | Lint suite                | `make lint`     | ✅     |
  | Unit tests                | `make test`     | ✅     |
  | Coverage ≥ 80%            | `make coverage` | ✅     |

  ---

  ## ✅ Checklist
  - [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
  - [x] Tests added/updated for changes
  - [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
  - [x] No secrets or credentials committed

  ---

  ## 📓 Notes (optional)

  **New files:**
  - `plugins/json_prune/__init__.py` — module marker
  - `plugins/json_prune/json_prune.py` — plugin implementation (handles both plain JSON   
  strings and MCP `content[0]["text"]` dicts)
  - `plugins/json_prune/plugin-manifest.yaml` — manifest
  - `plugins/json_prune/README.md` — documentation with config examples
  - `tests/unit/.../json_prune/test_json_prune.py` — 21 test cases across 6 test classes  

  **Modified:** `plugins/config.yaml` — registered plugin at priority 149 (after
  `json_repair` at 145), mode `disabled` by default.

  **Design decisions:**
  - Whitelist-only approach using dot-notation paths (e.g. `results.title`)
  - Webhook `name` key matches the contributor's original config format for compatibility 
  - No new dependencies — uses existing `orjson`
  - Immutable payload handling following `json_repair` pattern
